summary:
Diyarbakır stands under the national legal framework applying throughout Türkiye. Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 that a leaked draft of Türkiye's 11th Judicial Package would amend penal-code article 225 to punish conduct 'contrary to biological sex' with up to three years in prison, and would allow charges against anyone taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony, carrying up to four years.

The same draft would, under civil-code article 40, raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care from 18 to 25 and impose a permanent-infertility mandate; providers would face fines and up to seven years' imprisonment and patients up to three years. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected, and Human Rights Watch called for the draft's withdrawal. Whether the package has since been enacted is unresolved in the sources.

The source records no Diyarbakır-specific enforcement actions, incidents, or institutions bearing on trans visitors; the assessment for the city rests on the national framework.
tangentialFactors:
The draft provisions would apply uniformly across Türkiye's provinces, so a trans visitor in Diyarbakır faces the same statutory exposure as elsewhere in the country, with no regional variation documented.

The 11th Judicial Package sits within a broader pattern of legislative and executive hostility toward LGBT people reported by Human Rights Watch and other monitors, rather than as an isolated measure.
localsOnly:
Residents of Diyarbakır, including trans residents, would be directly subject to the draft penal-code and civil-code amendments described above if enacted, with the age-25 infertility-linked restriction on gender-affirming care affecting local access to medical treatment.

No province-specific detention, policing, or protection-machinery data for Diyarbakır appears in the source inventory.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since the 29 October 2025 report is unresolved in the sources.

No Diyarbakır-specific enforcement, incident, or institutional data was available in the inventory; the record relies on the national framework.
